title: A useless degree that still pays
hook: The degree teaches nothing. Firms still pay more for it, and they aren't wrong. How?

doesNotKnow: that a credential can pay even if it teaches nothing, because it costs able people less to earn

misconception: A degree is only worth getting if it makes you more productive.
objective: The learner can explain that because the degree costs able workers $20k and others $60k, only the able find it worth it ($80k vs $50k; $40k vs $50k), so holding one reveals ability and paying holders $100k is correct, though the degree teaches nothing.

claims.text: With the degree, able workers net $100k - $20k = $80k against $50k without; the others net $100k - $60k = $40k, less than $50k.
claims.source: 100 - 20 = 80 > 50; 100 - 60 = 40 < 50. Demo.tsx net(), takes(); re-run in node (ncm-e00). | FC pass 22 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): 100-20 = 80 > 50; 100-60 = 40 < 50; net(), takes() and reveal match.

claims.text: So only the able get the degree; holding one reveals ability, and firms are right to pay holders $100k though nobody learned a thing.
claims.source: From c1: every holder is able and produces $100k, so the $100k pay matches output. Stage message 'Only the able get it: the degree reveals ability.' | FC pass 22 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): with costs 20/60 only the able take it, so every holder produces 100 and pay 100 matches output; stage message 'Only the able get it: the degree reveals ability.'

claims.text: If the degree costs the others less than $50k, they get it too, and firms pay $100k to workers who produce $50k: the degree stops meaning anything; it signals ability only because it costs the able less to earn.
claims.source: Others take it when 100 - cost > 50, i.e. cost < 50 (preset $40k: 60 > 50). Demo.tsx takes(); stage message for the pooling state. | FC pass 22 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): takes(c) iff 100 - c > 50 iff c < 50; preset $40k: 60 > 50, both types take it (with able at 20), status 'pool', message 'firms pay $100k for $50k workers'. At exactly 50 the stage says 'tie: skips'.

claims.text: This is Spence's job-market signalling model.
claims.source: Spence 1973, 'Job Market Signaling', Quarterly Journal of Economics 87(3); Easley and Kleinberg 2010, ch. 22. Fact-checker to confirm. | FC pass 22 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Spence, 'Job Market Signaling', QJE 87(3):355-374 (1973) confirmed bibliographically via search (JSTOR record); not opened. A costless-to-output education that separates types only through differing costs is Spence's model (knowledge). E&K ch. 22 placement (asymmetric information / signalling sections after the lemons market): moderately confident from memory, section unconfirmed; not shown to learners.

claims.text: The lesson is a simplified model with invented numbers (two types, a fixed firm pay rule, ties skip the degree); it does not claim real degrees teach nothing.
claims.source: Assumptions of Demo.tsx; stage chip 'Model: the degree teaches nothing' and the reveal's last line. Lesson rule from the brief (claim 4). | FC pass 22 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Demo.tsx constants and rules (two types, fixed pay rule, tie skips); chip and muted reveal line match.

recall.question: A certificate teaches nothing. Holders are paid $30k more. It costs strong workers $10k and weak workers $40k. Who gets it?
recall.why: Strong workers gain $30k - $10k = $20k; weak workers would lose $40k - $30k = $10k. Only the strong get it, so it signals strength.
